So I don't actually hate this...

As at the bleeding edge, it is currently:

[1.2.3](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x10-V1-Architecture.md#v12-authentication-architecture)

> Verify that the application uses a single vetted authentication mechanism that is known to be secure, can be extended to include strong authentication, and has sufficient logging and monitoring to detect account abuse or breaches.

I would be tempted at this point to clarify it a little to say:

> Verify that the application uses a single authentication mechanism consistently. The mechanism should be well known/security tested, should support strong authentication, and should provide sufficient logging and monitoring functionality to detect account abuse or breaches.

Alternatively, it could be split:

> Verify that the application uses a single authentication mechanism consistently. 

> Verify that the application's authentication mechanism is well known and trusted or has undergone provable security testing.

> Verify that the application's authentication mechanism supports strong authentication

> Verify that the application's authentication mechanism provides sufficient logging and monitoring functionality to detect account abuse or breaches.

Thoughts?
